platforms.title: The Wound God Called His Own - 500 Years Early
platforms.description:
A Roman soldier raised his spear on a Friday afternoon - and finished a sentence God had started writing five hundred years earlier.

In Zechariah 12, the LORD himself is speaking, and he claims the wound as his own: "and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son" (Zechariah 12:10, KJV).

Look upon ME. Mourn for HIM. The pierced one is the LORD himself, come in the flesh. John stood at the cross, watched the spear go in, and reached for that old sentence (John 19:37). The soldier saw a dying man. John saw God keeping his own word.

And the promise begins with grace: grace poured out, not wrath: "the spirit of grace and of supplications." He gives the tears he asks for.

Do what the verse says. Look at him - and live.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Zechariah Saw the Cross - Five Centuries Before It Stood
platforms.description:
Five hundred years before Rome raised a cross outside Jerusalem, the prophet Zechariah wrote down a sentence that should stop every reader: the LORD himself says, "and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son" (Zechariah 12:10, KJV).

Look upon ME - the speaker is God. Mourn for HIM - the pierced one stands distinct. Inside one verse, the wound belongs to the LORD, and the LORD is the one who comes in the flesh to bear it.

At the crucifixion, the apostle John watched a Roman spear pierce Jesus' side - and he reached straight for Zechariah's sentence: "They shall look on him whom they pierced" (John 19:37). The soldier saw a dying man. John saw God keeping his own word.

And notice how the promise opens: not with wrath poured out, but "I will pour upon the house of David... the spirit of grace and of supplications." God gives the very tears he asks for. He did not send a stranger to be wounded for us. He came himself.

In this piece: the prophecy in its own context, the first-person mystery inside the Hebrew sentence, John's eyewitness use of it, and what it means to look at the pierced one today.

Look at him. Let grace turn looking into mourning, and mourning into trust. Look, and live.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- youtube_short + youtube_long + facebook descriptions: the SECOND quotation is an
  ELIDED verse quote - grace poured out, not wrath: "the spirit of grace and of supplications."
  The KJV reads "And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of
  Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications". Quoting with an internal
  ellipsis inside quote marks risks the verbatim-KJV gate and invites the "they
  edited the verse" objection. FIX: quote only the contiguous verbatim phrase -
  e.g. and the promise begins with grace: "the spirit of grace and of supplications"
  - or paraphrase without quote marks ("the promise opens with grace poured out,
  not wrath").
- youtube_short title "The Wound God Called His Own - 500 Years Early": honest and
  strong, but "500 Years Early" reads slightly like ad copy. Acceptable; note the
  narration itself says "over five hundred years", so "500 Years Early" stays
  truthful only as a floor - do not inflate to "exactly 500".
- tiktok: first line is good; hashtag set is broad-only. FIX: swap one broad tag for
  a niche one (#Zechariah1210 or #JesusInTheOldTestament) to earn the right feed.
- youtube_long tag list includes "awakeden" (brand, not a search keyword a stranger
  types). Harmless, but replace with "spear pierced side of jesus" or "zechariah
  prophecy explained" for actual search value.
- No clickbait, no doctrinal overclaim, primary anchor quote IS verbatim KJV,
  thread matches the video, platform tones are differentiated. After the elided-quote
  fix this kit passes.
